caption_en: 1. Facciaia in opus iîncertum, with holes in the beams of the canopy and a terracotta mask.   81 FU26835
2. Peristyle (1): O portico with arches turned on columns, S portico with two brick columns, N wall frescoed with garden painting.  81 FU26837
3. Peristyle (1): O portico with arches and cistern mouth, S portico with the S arch of the O portico incorporated, wall E with blind arches. Sketch by M. Oliva.  79 N56587

4. Peristyle (1), wall N: painting of a garden with a blue background within red and yellow windows with rostrum, helmet and lion head, behind a pluteus with red niches with the bases of the four fountains supported by a centaur or crouching sphinx, arranged symmetrically. Bases, support and fountain basins are painted as if they were carved in white marble. The cocciopesto channel that was supposed to collect rainwater at the foot of the N wall was illusionistically filled by the four painted fountains. AFS A8873

5. Peristyle (1), wall N, section O: garden painting on a blue background inside a large red window bordered by a garland and with a helmet and a lion head, behind a pluteus with a mask in the center and a pluteus with scales. Between these two is the base adorned with bearded heads, on which rests a centaur with a rudder in the right, patera in the left and a square fountain basin on the head. 77 N35840
6. Peristyle (1), N wall, W section. The Centaur that functions as a support for the fountain basin in the garden, holds a rudder.  77 N35844

7. Peristyle (1), wall N. The second large window from the W, in the center of which the fountain-carrying sphinx is crouching, is bordered at the top by two arches between which a mask is hung. On the yellow pilaster to the right of the window is painted a rostrum, a trophy of a sea battle. Between the hoof and the middle area, the joint of the pontate clearly appears.  77 N35841

8. Peristyle (1), N wall, second window from W. The base on which the labrum is placed, supported by a winged sphinx, is adorned with bearded heads. The sphinx recurs more often as a fountain support in gardens than the centaur: for example in houses VII 6,28; IX 2.7; IX 8.6; and in the villa of Oplontis.  AFS D8633
9. Peristyle (1), wall N. The mask hanging in the center of the second window from O, looking in the same direction as that of the sphinx below.  77 N35850

10. Peristyle (1), N wall: detail of the central yellow pilaster adorned with a rostrum. The painted shadow of the rostrum on the pilaster is in harmony with the natural source of light, beating the wall from S-W.  77 N35848
11. Peristyle (1), N wall, second window from E with sphinx crouching fountain holder.   AFS A8543

12. Peristyle (1), N wall, section E: large window with centaur crouching fountain. The red pilaster O is decorated with a helmet and a lion's head, the yellow pilaster E with bucranium and patera.  77 N35843
13. Peristyle (1), N wall, section E: trophy helmet hanging from the red pilaster.  777 N35847
14. Peristyle (1), N wall, section E: bucranium hanging as a sacral object from the yellow pilaster.  77 N35849

15. Peristyle (1), N wall, section E. The square fountain supported by the crouching centaur with rudder and patera is adorned with heads at the corners. Similar centaurs are found in the painted gardens in the villa of Oplontis, perhaps to be attributed to the same workshop.  AFS A8876

16. Peristyle (1), wall E. The blind arch was also painted with a garden, preceded by a pluteus with a black background with a swan in the center: paint applied over the layer of plaster of the previous decoration, tapped-for the adhesion of the overlapping layer. The columns are covered with yellow plaster, with the capital adorned with stucco frames with tongues. AFS A8870
17. Peristyle (1), portico S, column E: the abacus plastered in white adorned with a purple border.  77 N35874

18. Peristyle (1), S portico, S wall, section W with the window of the room (3). Black plinth decoration, black middle area with a painting flanked by candelabra (which has become illegible without ever being documented); the upper white area bears a border of triangle carpet.  77 N35873

19. Peristyle (1), West porch, S wall, W section with the cubicle door (7). The hoof and the middle area are black; The panels of the middle area are interrupted at the frames of the cubicle door.  The pilaster in the corner is adorned with a stretched garland. The oblique course of the upper area follows the line of the sloping roof of the porch. 77 N35857
20. Peristyle (1), West portico, S wall, middle area to the right of the entrance to the cubicle (7): small picture depicting a vase on a high pedestal.  777 N35860
21. Peristyle (1), West portico, S section with arches. AFS D2331

22. Peristyle (1), wall O, central section: niche of arched lararium frescoed on a white background with roses in the intrados and with the togato Genius of the master of the house, or of the family, in the act of freeing himself from the patera on the circular altar. He holds a cornucopia in his left hand and is assisted by a boy in a short two-club tunic with a pitcher in his right. On the altar hang two woolen puppets offered to the Lares on the occasion of the feast of the compitalia. 77 N35858
23. Peristyle (1), portico W, column N: the abacus consisting of a tile, is covered with a stucco frame with tongues.   77 N35859
24. Room (2), S wall with room door (5), crank staircase and balcony. Sketch by M. Oliva.  79 N56561

25. Room (2), painted S wall with a red plinth, red middle area divided into two parts by a yellow twisted candelabrum flanked by cupids in flight, and white upper area with an oblique garland.  77 N35869
26. Room (3), N wall frescoed with a yellow plinth with two tufts, and a yellow middle area (blazed by the red-hot eruptive material) divided into two parts by a silver candelabrum.  77 N35870

27. Cubicle (7), N wall: white middle area with bird in the O-panel of the door; white upper area with bird perched on the garland above the edge of a carpet in semicircles and triangles;  white bezel with white stucco moulded frame.  '77 N35868

28. Cubicle (7), S wall: red plinth; white middle area with central aedicule with a painting depicting Narcissus and side panel E with bird (section W has been pierced by ancient tunnels). Under the white lunette there is a molded frame of white stucco.  77 N35866

29. Cubicle (7), S wall, middle area, central section: painting depicting the hunter Narcissus seated, characterized by the spear arranged diagonally in accordance with the position of the figure, intent on aiming at his own image reflected from the source. The handsome Narcissus will be punished by the gods, who will turn him into a flower for rejecting the nymph Echo; The nymph appears at the top right.  77 N35861

30. Cubicle (7), W wall: red plinth; white middle area with a central aedicule, which preserves the coffered ceiling rendered in perspective and the painting in the center of a carpet bordered by a band of staples, which presents a figure of a woman (Venus?) seated in the act of fishing in front of a cupid. The carpet edges of the side panels adorned with a bird and with an acroterial dolphin, turn the corner continuing on the other wall. In the center of the upper white area stands a leafy aedicule with a shell-shaped basin.   7°7 N35867

31. Cubicle (7), W wall, middle area, central panel.  In ten out of the twenty cases in which the Fisher Venus appears in Pompeii - always in paintings of the fourth style, always in cubicles - the goddess is the pendant to a painting with Narcissus. A shell covers the leafy aedicule in the upper area above the central painting of the photo.  77 N35862
32. Cubicle (7), W wall, middle area, N. The bird with cherries is also part of the erotic imagery of the cubicle [cf. I 12, 3, cubicle (3)].  7°7 N35863
33. Cubicle (7), W wall, middle area, S section. The dolphin sacred to the sea Venus (Aphrodite Pelàgia) is an acroterium also inserted in the context of a cubicle decoration.   '77 N35864

1. Caupona of the Gladiator. Garden (1), section N-E: public summer triclinium (?), which was perhaps a caupona. The wine consumed there was probably produced by the adjoining vineyard. The door and window with railings in the N wall communicate with the workshop of the oil furnaces I 20, 3; Next to the door is the water tank pillar.  According to a hypothesis by the excavator A. Maiuri, the tanks behind the masonry triclinium served as a fish nursery.   AFS D2175

2. Garden (1). View from above from the W with the summer triclinium, the staircase that went up to the house of the innkeeper who produced oil lamps located above the kiln workshop, the room for crushing grapes in the N-E corner with the basement and altar in front of the S pillar, four dolii and the base of the statue of the gladiator, in tuff.  And 108839
3. Garden (1). The tuff statue of the gladiator at the time of discovery.  AFS D2175
4. Garden (1). View of the summer triclinium with the N wall and the window railing, the pillar of the water tank and dolii when the excavation was completed.  AFS D3619

5. Garden (1) with the horseshoe-shaped counter of the masonry triclinium covered with cocciopesto plaster, and the niches under the counter to store food. The hollow in the triclinium table communicates with the cistern below. AFS D3617 6. 6. Workshop: the minor two-chamber oven in opus incertum in the S-E corner, with the interior and the façade in brick.  77 N36487
1. Officina dilucerne: the two-chamber oven in the N-W corner, with the upper chamber covered by an amphora vault.  Sketch by M. Oliva.  79 N56606

2. Workshop, oil lamp kiln in the N-W corner: brick oven façade with an apotropaic stucco phallus near the lower arch. Similar phalluses are often found near the mouths of ovens in bakeries (VI 6, 17), dyeing plants (IX 7, 2) and spas (II 4, 4).  AFS A8855
3. Workshop, oil lamp furnace in the N-W corner: lower chamber with bivalve matrices of skylight.   AFS D923
4. Workshop: the reverberation plane with holes of the upper chamber of the oven in corner 77 N36488
5. Workshop: the amphorae in the vault of the upper chamber of the oven in the N-W corner. AFS D742 1069

7. Workshop: minor kiln in the S-E corner: the reverberation plane with holes in the upper chamber in brick.  77 N36490

1. Façade in opus incertum with lava threshold and tuff sofa capitals, with the right jamb of the entrance restored with opus listatum of a row of bricks and one of tuff blocks after the earthquake of 62 AD.  80 N56692

2. Façade: tuff sofa capital of jamb S composed of the talus at the base, a palmette between two shoots with a bellflower seen from the front and the spool under the abacus. The right section of the capital is chipped, probably due to the collapse of the wooden architrave. 80 N56688

3. Façade: the tuff sofa capital of jamb N is of the same workmanship as that of jamb S, and is better preserved.  The ornament on the shaded side in the shape of a sofa, which was originally supposed to face the street, is chiselled, perhaps because it was damaged by the earthquake of 62 AD. The two capitals will have been swapped and turned with the healthy face on the outside. This type of capital dates back to at least the second century BC.  80 N56690
4. Atrium(2): N side, reinforced with two pillars in opus mixtum of two rows of bricks and one of limestone blocks after the earthquake of 62 AD.  AFS D2294
5. Atrium (2), S wall: paratactic stucco relief decoration in the first style, with pilasters that mark the wall "behind" in an illusionistic way. 77 N36494
6. Atrium (2), S wall, section O: decoration in the first style with pilaster and plinth surmounted by a floor and orthostats. All colors have disappeared except the red of the top.  77 N36493

7. Cubicle (7) converted into kitchen and latrine, corner NO.  The cocciopesto floor is adorned with a dotted white tesserae in the area under the bed, a double meandering bedside rug and a diamond carpet outlined with white tesserae in the antechamber. The wall is decorated in stucco relief in the first style, with the plinth adorned with perspective cubes surmounted by a faux alabaster top and ashlars. The kitchen counter and 1 latrine table supports leaning against the N wall were already collapsed in 1977, together with the N wall.  AFS D2298
8. Cubicle (7), transformed into a kitchen, section N: counter with tiles walled up along the edge.   AFS D2293

9. Cubicle (7), wall E. Of the plinth with perspective cubes the small piece next to the door remains; the upper area is made up of three rows of ashlars, surmounted by a small floor and a kyma of stucco that is now colorless. The beams of the floor were housed in the circular holes.  80 N57612

10. Cubicle (7), wall E, plinth, section N of the door. What remains of the decoration with perspective cubes, the contours of which were engraved in the still damp plaster before being colored.  80 N57614

2. Façade in opus incertum: the N-W corner with the limestone track slab carved with an apotropaic all. The Romans considered corners particularly exposed to dangers, capable of rising from all sides. 77 N36495

3. Garden (2), wall N, in opus incertum with circular holes for the beams of a sloping roof and amphorae incorporated at the top of the wall to raise it without weighing it down and preventing access to outsiders.  77 N36504

4. Garden (2), wall N, central section with a door jamb of parallelepiped blocks of limestone walled with opus încertum, and the circular holes for the beams of a sloping roof under the amphorae incorporated at the top of the wall.  77 N36505

1. Room (1), wall N. Rich decoration with a red plinth and, in the middle area, stretched carpets tied with bows and bordered by garlands. Architectural views with thòloi adorned with metal antefixes appear between the panels. IV style.   7°7 N36508
2. Room (l), wall E. The motifs on wall N return here; The central panel is not legible. IV style.  77 N36496

3. Room (1), wall W. It preserves the complex decoration of the upper area, with a white background, with pergolas, stones, garlands and the remains of a drapery gura. The gaps filled with concrete must have contained other decorative elements, as evidenced by a photo taken in the 60s, in which above the central panel appear two peacocks facing two lyres. IV style. 77N36511

4. Room (1), wall O, section S, middle area: architectural view with a twisted candelabrum. The decorated leaves of the open door are rendered with great care, as is the whole decoration of the room, which is probably to be attributed to the initial phase of the IV style.  77 N36507

5. Room (The), wall O, section S, middle area: the architectural foreshortening contains a coffered ceiling with a valley adorned with antefixes; in the foreground a golden twisted candelabrum. IV style.  77 N36510

6. Room (1), wall W, central section. White upper area: carpet edges in alternating circles and triangles, swans holding garlands in their beaks, oblique thyrsis and stylized dolphins.  IV style.  77 N36509
7. Room (1), wall W, section N. The negative trace of the cupid that adorned the yellow carpet of the middle area.  IV style.  77 N36514
8. Room (1), wall O, section N. Pantera above the stretched carpet of the middle area.IV style.  77 N36512
9. Room (1), wall W, section N. The garland of vine leaves that hangs behind the twisted candelabrum is one of the finest examples executed during the era of the fourth style.  77 N36513

1. Caupona (1), serving counter, N front frescoed with fake marble incrustation: "in the centre, a disc of antique yellow in a porphyry square; two narrow vertical rectangles, on the sides, of white marble veined with green serpentine lozenges; then squares of white veined in a field of green serpentine; then again, at the ends, two narrow vertical rectangles of antique yellow: all terminated, at the top, by a band of white marble and, at the bottom, by a red plinth". At the bottom you can see the three steps "intended to accommodate crockery and glasses for drinks", "painted red and threaded in white". (Spinazzola NS 1917, p. 250).
2. Caupona (1), bar, W side frescoed on a red background with squares, including oblique thyrsis and hanging garlands.

3. Façade, jamb to the E of entrance II 1, 1 to the caupona (1): "On a red background [...] a Mercury on the right with a yellow caduceus on the left. leaning out and pouch in the d., partly dressed in fluttering blue veils, her winged hair" (Della Corte NS 1919, p. 232).

4. Kitchen (3), wall S, section E above the masonry counter. The opus încertum walls of the kitchen were covered with rough plaster, with a special layer of smooth white plaster applied on top for painting the Lares. These appear, as usual, in a symmetrical group with the outer hand raised to pour the wine from the rhytòn into the situla held in the other, lowered hand. The altar and the offerer depicted among the Lares are surmounted by a two-handled tabula with the dedication Felix Laribus / con [se] c [rat] votum (CIL IV 9887). Above the stage a wreath

5. Viridarium (5), wall E seen from N-W. The wall that divides the garden once shared between houses II 1, l1ell1,2, is crowned by a dense series of upside-down amphorae, broken, except for the last one to the S. The presence of a gabled structure can be deduced from the gaps left in the white plaster covering the wall.

6. Façade on the W alley of the caupona. The side entrance to the house behind the room (at no. 13) had a barely legible representation to the N of the lintel of the door: these are two male figures seen in profile in a symmetrical position exerting force on a vertical stick, with four clypei hanging above their heads.

1. Back room (2), W wall. The black plinth was divided into compartments adorned with corolla and bucranium, which have now disappeared. The middle area includes two red panels with a vignette depicting a lion rampant towards the centre, which simulates a 'window' with a white background above the yellow partition with a brown corolla in the centre of the wall. From the goblet crater placed on the windowsill emerges a floral arrangement tapering upwards, with a bird perched on top. A painting depicting an architectural landscape remains of the upper white area.

2. Back room (2), W wall, S section, middle area, detail: yellow rampant lion on a red background. The motif recurs several times in the decorations of the Painters' Workshop in Via di Castricio, for example in the nearby House of D. Octavius Quartio (II, 2,2), room (e). 77 N39220

3. Backroom (2), wall E. The plaster remaining on the wall is from the ancient basement and follows the course of the wooden staircase, which was resting on the three-step masonry podium in the N-E corner of the room. The shopkeepers lived în pergulis (i.e. above the shop), if they had not used the first floor as a warehouse (as in the case of the balcony above the caupona II 1, 1). The black hoof is adorned with a corolla and bucranium. Despite the position of the staircase, the middle area follows the scheme applied to the opposite wall, without any modification: a norm followed in all Roman houses.

4. Back room (2), wall E, central section, middle area, detail: yellow partition with brown corolla, surmounted by the 'window' with a shiny metal goblet crater. Two shoots fall from the floral composition, towards which two phoenixes are heading.
5. Caupona II 1, 6 (1): "pillar overlooking the entrance, to the left of the window" (Della Corte NS 1958, p. 117). Red plaster with graffiti (MAXIM IRENAE SVI[AJE).  AFS A1569 (formerly A8732)

1. Viridarium (1), with entrance from no. 9, wall E. The finer plaster around the lararium niche with two corinth-shaped pillars and a triangular tympanum made of stucco in colored relief, is applied over the rough plaster that covers the walls of the garden. The photograph taken with grazing light reveals the volume of the body of the stucco sea monster that filled the surface of the tympanum. The two frescoed panels above appear adorned with garlands and birds with spread wings. Excavation photo 1954.

2. Viridarium (1), wall E. The larium at the end of the excavation is already less conspicuous than in the previous photo, made halfway through the excavation. The plinth below the niche has a garden painting adorned with garlands; the altar and the snake in the middle of the garden are executed in stucco relief. The bottom of the niche is painted with faux numidian marble; the tympanum has a frame with heart-shaped scrolls. In the middle area, between the niche and the window of the room (3), Hercules appears with a crowned head, resting on the club covered by the lion and with the sk}phos in his right hand lowered, according to the well-known type created by Lysippus (Heracles Farnese). AFS A1573 (formerly A8736)
1. Room (2), E. Wall Red plinth with plants; Yellow middle area with central compartment and side panels.

2. Room (2), S wall, section E, with the window with large limestone jambs open towards the garden (10). In an earlier phase, the room took light from the garden through a smaller window located at a higher level, later walled up. The simple decoration features a red plinth adorned with a panel with plants and a yellow paneled middle area, which has now almost completely collapsed. IV style.
3. Room (2), wall S, section E. Red panel with plants. IV style.
4. Room (3), wall N. Almost nothing remains of the red background decoration of the plinth and the middle area.
5. Room (3), wall N, section E. Detail of the edges of a triangle carpet and the architectural foreshortening with a hanging garland. IV style.

6. Room (3), wall O, with a bipartite scheme: in the center of the wall, adorned with a red plinth and a central area, also red, is a compartment with a candelabrum; side panels with checkered and carpet edges. IV style.
7. Room (3), wall O, section S. Picture vanished. IV style.

8. Room (4), wall N. The wall, very short, also bears a bipartite scheme; In the center of the black plinth is a narrow compartment with plants, flanked by wider panels with the same subject. The center of the middle area is instead marked only by a blue band lined with white; the side panels are bordered by carpet edges with two parallel lines. IV style.
9. Room (4), N wall, section O. Panel with plants in the plinth with a black background.
10. Room (4), N wall,
11. Room (4), O wall. Remains of a fresco of the fourth style with black plinth and red middle area.

12. Room (7), wall N. remains of fresco, most likely of the IV style, with red plinth and yellow middle area. The fresco is executed above the infill of a door that communicated with the uncovered area (1) of the adjoining house II 1, 11.
13. Room (7), wall S to W of the door open to the corridor (6). Red hoof and yellow middle area. IV style?

14. Room (7), wall W with window and the door connecting with the room (4), (of which the plastered jambs can be glimpsed), also transformed into a window. The decoration, with a red plinth and a yellow middle area, can probably be dated to the fourth style, like all the others preserved in the house.

1. Façade, front door jamb N. In the finer, white plaster square, specially applied to the rough plaster covering the façade, there is a Venus who has just come out of the water (symbolized by the dolphin behind her), fixing her hair. Amor sitting on his shoulder, helps his mother hold the mirror, which is turned so that we see the reflected image of Venus' face. Hips and legs are wrapped in the cloak, from which the goddess emerges bare-chested; A polychrome garland hangs from the corners of the painting. The plaster that turns the corner is painted with a Priapus almost completely vanished.

2. Façade, S-panel of the entrance door, depicting Mercury handing the pouch to those who enter, and having the caduceus in his left. The god of gain is in the company of Dionysus who carries a glass (?) in his lowered right hand and thyrsus in his left, with which he also holds his cloak. The two deities who promise all the material, gastronomic and soteriological good, are the pendant to the Venus on the N jamb of the entrance door to the complex, and they also appear under a polychrome garland.

3. Inside of the $12 front door jamb. Priapus, son of Venus and Dionysus, holds with both hands the fruit contained in the folds of the dress gathered over the erect phallus, his weapon, which must protect property, in particular the hortus. His (double) presence on the jambs next to the boundary is, therefore, of a strategic order, to be compared with the position of Priapus in the vestibule of the House of the Vettii (VI 15, 1). The god of Lampsacus is bearded and has hair sprouting from under a striped cloth handkerchief (cf. the Dionysian masks painted in the atrium of the House of Theatrical Pictures: vol. I, fig.29a p.378).

4a-b. Triclinium (3), S. The black hoof is adorned with plants, birds and insects. On the right there is a recess to accommodate the headboard of the lectus medius, the bed placed between the two others of the triclinium. The central panel of the middle area, verdigris with a red border, is flanked by yellow panels with a black border between red panels with a yellow border. The brightly colored panels are separated by white pillars adorned with ivy leaves. The white frame between the middle and upper areas has triple stylized ornaments, i.e. a geometrical lotus flower above each pillar, and a group of two triangles flanking a painted drop on the axis of each panel of the middle area. The still lifes in the white panels of the upper area refer to the function of the room as a banquet hall.

9. Triclinium (3), S wall, central section, upper area, detail: still life. From the upside-down basket with two handles, dates come out on a support, and on the shelf below.

The dividing walls between the ecus (5), the room (6) and the room to the W of it, leaning against the perimeter walls of the complex in limestone opus incertum, were made in opus craticium with a wooden frame, as shown by the square mirrors that belonged to the plinth of those walls. In the small room, it was preferred not to emphasize the center of the wall with a painting and instead a bipartite decorative scheme was chosen, a solution frequently adopted in the case of small rooms. The name painted below the figure, read by various editors as Amulius Faventinus/Tiburs, or Loreius Tiburtinus, is at the origin of one of the modern names attributed to the house.

65. Oecus (h), wall E; S wall, E section. The photo, which also includes the section to the left of the S door that overlooks the garden, allows us to follow the narrative sequence of the frieze of the episode of Hercules in 'Troy' which culminates in the investiture of Priam, Hesio's younger brother, of the kingship of Troy. Since the scene was in Nero's Domus Transitoria in Rome, it is not unlikely that the episode, which has become topical, began to circulate among the municipal elites. The insula perhaps belonged to an augustalis (as could also be deduced from the civic crown between two branches or laurel trees in the overdoor at no. 4: see II 2, 4, figs. 1-2) whose tasks included the spread of imperial ideology.

For the occasion he is dressed in a white cloak without giving up the lion: whose tail falls in front of Hesion's left foot, in a symmetrical position with respect to that of the naked Hercules seen from behind to the right with the quiver tied to his left side, while brandishing the bow (creating a suggestion of depth). Oecus (h), wall E, section S, middle area, black predella, detail (below the wedding of Hesio): a Trojan seated on the ground with his hands folded on his right knee, perhaps the herald Ideo, keeps company with Priam slumped seen from behind while they guard the ransomed body of Hector (who does not appear). The two figures seem to be illuminated by the glare of a fire lit in the night. The tent of Achilles follows, sitting in front of a clypeus while the old pedagogue Phoenix, kneeling, begs him to renounce his anger and bring help to the army of the Achaeans. At the S end of the wall, Achilles sits in front of his tent, his right hand resting under his chin in a pensive attitude, disposing of his anger (mènis) for Agamemnon's offense: the leitmotif of the Iliad.
74. Oecus(h), E wall, S section, middle area, black predella, detail: Priam.

75. Oecus (h), wall S to E of the door, middle area, frieze, detail: Hercules seated with his club covered by the lion placed under his left armpit, transmits the royal power of Troy to Priam, placing the Phrygian cap on his head. The little boy accepts: he touches the cap with his right hand, while his left clutches the scepter.
